questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: c = 16.4f * (12 + 16.4f) / (16.4f - 12). Console.WriteLine of that float prints 105.85455 (binary float is not exactly 16.4).

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: Operators / and * have higher precedence than + and -. 1) b/3 = 5. 2) c*2 = 6. 3) x = 90 - 5 + 6 - 1 = 90.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: Step 1: Parentheses (3*2)=6 and (80+2)=82. Step 2: x = 80 - 15 / 6 * 82. Step 3: Integer division 15 / 6 = 2. Step 4: 80 - (2 * 82) = 80 - 164 = -84.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the precedence of arithmetic operators in C#?

options.text: Multiplicative (*, /, %) have higher precedence than Additive (+, -)
Additive (+, -) have higher precedence than Multiplicative (*, /, %)
Modulo (%) has higher precedence than Division (/)
All arithmetic operators have the same precedence

questions.explanation: In C#, multiplication, division, and remainder operators have equal precedence and are higher than addition and subtraction.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: Iteration 1: j=1. k = (j++) - (++j) = 1 - 3 = -2 (j becomes 3). Iteration 2: j=3. k = 3 - 5 = -2 (j becomes 5). Iteration 3: j=5. k = 5 - 7 = -2 (j becomes 7).

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct way to use a compound assignment operator for incrementing by 1 in C#?
questions.explanation: The operator '+=' is a compound assignment operator. 'c += 1' is equivalent to 'c = c + 1'.
